slides.title: Mercedes' title night, three voices.
slides.sub: The league, the team and the rival each told the São Paulo GP differently.

slides.body: “All it takes is all of us”: the champions put the whole team in the frame, not one driver. The caption says “NINTH time”.
slides.tip: Hypothesis: a team photo shares the credit with the people fans never see.

slides.body: Same race, opposite approach: one driver, a giant “Winner” and a race-result tag. It out-liked Mercedes' title post.
slides.tip: Hypothesis: a single face is easier to celebrate than a team.

slides.title: McLaren congratulated, on Mercedes' post
slides.body: McLaren's “Congratulations! 🧡” on the Mercedes title post drew 746 likes. Ferrari's comment drew 365. Brands such as adidas, WhatsApp, IWC and PepsiCo also commented.
slides.tip: Hypothesis: rival and sponsor comments turn the comment section into extra content.

slides.title: @f1 posted it too, at another scale
slides.body: The F1 title graphic got 1.5M likes and 3.5k comments, against 134.6k and 949 on the team's own post. Mercedes' own comments on it drew 2.2k and 2.9k likes.
slides.tip: Hypothesis: the league account brings an audience the team does not own.

slides.title: Two championships in three weeks
slides.body: After Kimi Antonelli's drivers' title in Mexico, Mercedes posted a “two championships in three weeks” reel, and earlier a prize call with Kimi on WhatsApp via the link in bio.
slides.tip: Hypothesis: linking a title to a brand activation keeps the celebration useful after the final whistle.

slides.title: Share the credit: a group photo works for a big team and for a small club alike.
Celebrate with partners: a rival, a sponsor or a league comment costs nothing and extends the post.

slides.big: See real club posts and why they worked.
